verses.text: A wise son heeds his father's discipline, but a mocker does not listen to rebuke.
From the fruit of his lips a man enjoys good things, but the desire of the faithless is violence.
He who guards his mouth protects his life, but the one who opens his lips invites his own ruin.
The slacker craves yet has nothing, but the soul of the diligent is fully satisfied.
The righteous hate falsehood, but the wicked bring shame and disgrace.
Righteousness guards the man of integrity, but wickedness undermines the sinner.
One pretends to be rich, but has nothing; another pretends to be poor, yet has great wealth.
Riches may ransom a man's life, but a poor man hears no threat.
The light of the righteous shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked is extinguished.
Arrogance leads only to strife, but wisdom is with the well-advised.
Dishonest wealth will dwindle, but what is earned through hard work will be multiplied.
Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but desire fulfilled is a tree of life.
He who despises instruction will pay the penalty, but the one who respects a command will be rewarded.
The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life, turning one from the snares of death.
Good understanding wins favor, but the way of the faithless is difficult.
Every prudent man acts with knowledge, but a fool displays his folly.
A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful envoy brings healing.
Poverty and shame come to him who ignores discipline, but whoever heeds correction is honored.
Desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but turning from evil is detestable to fools.
He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will be destroyed.
Disaster pursues sinners, but prosperity is the reward of the righteous.
A good man leaves an inheritance to his children's children, but the sinner's wealth is passed to the righteous.
Abundant food is in the fallow ground of the poor, but without justice it is swept away.
He who spares the rod hates his son, but he who loves him disciplines him diligently.
A righteous man eats to his heart's content, but the stomach of the wicked is empty.

context.author: Solomon, named in the heading “The proverbs of Solomon” (10:1). The collection runs from 10:1 to 22:16, about 375 sayings.
context.genre: Wisdom sayings: two-line proverbs, most of them contrasts
context.audience: Anyone learning to live wisely, first the young men of Israel’s court and households
context.mapLabel: JERUSALEM, THE ROYAL COURT OF SOLOMON
context.setting: These sayings are about words, work and the path a life takes. The one who guards his mouth protects his life (v.3); the slacker craves and has nothing, while the diligent are fully satisfied (v.4). Some pretend to be rich and have nothing; others pretend to be poor and have great wealth (v.7). “Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but desire fulfilled is a tree of life” (v.12). “He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will be destroyed” (v.20). The chapter ends with two well-known lines on raising children and on having enough (vv.24-25).
context.custom: Inheritance mattered greatly in Israel, where land passed down through families (Numbers 27:8-11); a good man leaves an inheritance to his grandchildren (v.22). Wealth gained quickly was distrusted (v.11). The rod (v.24) was the shepherd’s and teacher’s staff and the common tool of correction in the ancient world.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 14 sets the wise woman who builds her house beside the fool who tears hers down.
context.timelineBible: The land of Israel was the people’s inheritance from God (Joshua 13-21), and Naboth refused to sell his vineyard because it was his fathers’ inheritance (1 Kings 21:3). Hebrews 12:5-11 explains the Lord’s discipline as the love of a father.

translation.meaning: Expectation, waiting. Hope that keeps being put off wears down the heart.
Sharp, eager, hardworking. The diligent are the opposite of the slacker.
A staff or rod, also a scepter or a tribe. Here the tool of a parent’s correction.

gospelParallels.note: God disciplines us as sons, for our good.
Fathers, do not provoke your children; raise them in the Lord.

otBackground.note: Naboth will not sell his fathers’ inheritance.
Blessed is the man who does not walk with the wicked.

overview.summary: Guard your words, work hard, choose wise friends, and discipline your children; hope delayed hurts, but desire fulfilled is a tree of life.
overview.settingLine: Sayings about choices and their fruit.

customs.t: Friends shaped a young man’s path.

archaeology.t: Fields were marked with stones that could not be moved (Deuteronomy 19:14).
Bench tombs near Jerusalem held generations of one family.

overview.discussion: “He who walks with the wise will become wise” (v.20). Who are the people I walk with most, and what are they making of me?
overview.book: The book of Proverbs · 31 chapters. Short sayings and longer poems that teach how to live wisely in God’s world, beginning with the fear of the LORD.
overview.author: Solomon (10:1)
